title: The Nissan Patrol turns 75 after becoming the first vehicle to climb Mount Fuji
extract: Nissan marks 75 years of the Patrol, revisiting its 1958 Mount Fuji climb and previewing the new 2027 Armada Patrol PRO-4X with off-road hardware and adaptive air suspension.

title: Spyker returns with an 800-hp manual hypercar that targets Pagani and Bugatti
extract: A new Spyker is planned around a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8, a manual gearbox and an 800-hp target, with production intended to remain deliberately low-volume.

title: Ferrari 499P wins first Asian Le Mans Hypercar race at Paul Ricard
extract: AF Corse's Ferrari 499P took the opening Asian Le Mans Series Hypercar victory at Paul Ricard in a rain-affected four-hour race, giving Ferrari an early win in the new class.

title: Oscar Piastri: You have to manhandle McLaren's F1 car to find its potential
extract: Piastri says the MCL40 has to be driven at what feels like 110% to be quick, with its narrow performance window making it difficult to extract the car's full pace.

title: The Petrolhead Corner: Going off-road and beyond with three wild SEMA builds
extract: The feature tours three extreme SEMA projects, including a 1,300-hp hybrid Honda Passport Trophy Truck with an 800V system, alongside radical Nissan and Jeep builds.

title: McLaren to upgrade MCL40 at its bogey F1 track in Las Vegas
extract: McLaren plans to introduce MCL40 parts at Las Vegas, describing the work as a foundation for its 2027 car after recent gains in driveability and performance.

title: Linux 7.4-rc3 released with a broad set of late fixes
extract: The third release candidate for Linux 7.4 brings late fixes across drivers, filesystems and networking as the kernel approaches its final release.

title: AMD prepares capacity-aware scheduling for Linux hybrid CPUs
extract: AMD is preparing Linux scheduler support that exposes per-core capacity information for hybrid CPUs, helping the scheduler place work more intelligently across different core types.

title: IBM enables ARM64 guest virtual machines on s390
extract: IBM has outlined support for running ARM64 guest virtual machines on its s390 mainframe platform, a notable cross-architecture virtualization step for its Linux and KVM ecosystem.

title: AMD's ARG Root Guest feature for SEV-SNP VMs is coming to Linux
extract: AMD's ARG Root Guest design extends SEV-SNP confidential computing with a protected root guest that can coordinate virtual-machine operations such as live migration without requiring guest changes.

title: ASUS Ascent QN10 mini PC gets Linux support
extract: The Snapdragon X2 Elite-powered ASUS Ascent QN10 mini PC is gaining Linux support as developers bring up its firmware and platform devices.

title: Redox OS gets Go working and a GIMP port
extract: Redox OS's latest development update reports working Go toolchains and a GIMP port, alongside continued work on its Rust-based userspace and package-management improvements.

title: Basic Apple M5 support begins landing for Linux 7.5
extract: Initial Linux 7.5 device-tree support for Apple's M5 platform is landing, an early step toward booting Linux on the newest Apple silicon; GPU support remains a separate challenge.

title: Red Hat develops QEMU memory tiering for virtual machines
extract: Red Hat is developing QEMU memory-tiering support that can use NVMe-backed storage as a slower memory tier for virtual machines, potentially easing DRAM pressure on dense hosts.

title: FreeBSD 15.2-BETA2 released with OpenSSH and VirtIO updates
extract: FreeBSD 15.2-BETA2 brings OpenSSH 10.6p2, ML-DSA/Ed25519 host-key defaults and further VirtIO and networking fixes ahead of the stable release.

title: KDE Plasma 6.9 will allow XWayland to run on demand
extract: KDE Plasma 6.9 is set to launch XWayland only when needed, alongside new window-effect presets and other desktop refinements.

title: Thirty years ago in Dundee, the birth of Grand Theft Auto
extract: Le Monde revisits the small Dundee team behind the original Grand Theft Auto, tracing the game's origins and the design decisions that turned a top-down experiment into a landmark open-world series.

title: The original Xbox turns 25: the PC-derived console that challenged the PS2
extract: Tom's Hardware marks 25 years since the original Xbox launch, revisiting its Pentium III and Nvidia architecture, built-in hard drive and Ethernet as defining hardware choices.

title: DOSBox Staging posts a fresh development build
extract: The project's official development-build tracker lists a new 0.84.0-alpha-7d4b4 snapshot dated 14 November, giving MS-DOS emulation users another build to test.

title: RetroRecomp 1.7.6 expands support for classic platforms
extract: Version 1.7.6 adds support for Game Boy Advance, MSX2+, Nintendo 64, PlayStation and Amiga 1200, broadening the project's native recompilation pipeline across classic platforms.

title: Garbage brings generations together with its rock at Mexico City's Zócalo
extract: Around 90,000 people gathered at Mexico City's Zócalo for Garbage's free show, which brought together generations of fans and included a guest appearance by The Warning.

title: Foo Fighters deliver a sweary, high-energy spectacle at Marvel Stadium
extract: The band played a three-hour, 31-song set at Melbourne's Marvel Stadium, mixing catalogue favourites with a tribute to Taylor Hawkins and a showcase for new drummer Ilan Rubin.

title: Sunday Morning Showdown: Panerai Submersible Destro vs Omega Seamaster Ploprof
extract: Fratello pits Panerai's 44mm Submersible Marina Militare Destro PAM01757 against Omega's 1200m Seamaster Ploprof Summer Blue, comparing two distinctive professional dive-watch philosophies.

title: Modern escapement developments, part II
extract: SJX examines contemporary mechanical escapement experiments, from established manufacturers' latest designs to independent watchmakers challenging the traditional Swiss lever.

title: The ABCs of Time: dial styles, history and evolution of a watch's crucial part
extract: Monochrome traces the evolution of watch-dial styles, from early utilitarian layouts and railroad standards to California, military, Bauhaus and Art Deco designs.

title: Chopard Mille Miglia Classic Chronograph American Racing Stripes watch hands-on
extract: A hands-on look at Chopard's Mille Miglia Classic Chronograph in its American Racing Stripes edition, a motorsport-inspired treatment of the brand's long-running rally chronograph.

title: Hands-on: Nubeo Tranquility Automatic Star Trek 60th Anniversary watch
extract: A Blog to Watch goes hands-on with Nubeo's Tranquility Automatic Star Trek 60th Anniversary watch, a limited-edition tribute to the franchise's visual world.

title: The Auret Mederi: a distinctive debut with Colombian roots
extract: Fratello introduces the Auret Mederi, a new independent watch with Colombian roots, a distinctive multi-sided case and a deeply textured dial.

title: ‘It's like the wild west’: how AI has rocked the literary world
extract: The Guardian examines how generative AI is disrupting publishing, from questions of authorship and disclosure to the uncertainty facing writers, agents and editors.

title: She was a monster: the real Patricia Highsmith, by the people who knew her
extract: People who knew Patricia Highsmith describe the writer behind Tom Ripley, exploring the unsettling gap between her crime-fiction brilliance and her difficult private life.

title: The Sensualist by Gary Shteyngart review: a delectable romp through life's pleasures
extract: Gary Shteyngart's new essay collection gets a lively review, ranging across food, travel, watches and the small pleasures of everyday life with the author's trademark comic voice.

title: Saturday Night Live recap: is John Mulaney the best modern host we have?
extract: John Mulaney returns to host Saturday Night Live, and the recap argues that his tightly structured sketches and recurring characters make him one of the show's strongest modern hosts.

title: The DCU's James Gunn and Peter Safran have been fired: what next for superhero movies?
extract: The Guardian's Week in Geek assesses the reported exit of James Gunn and Peter Safran from DC Studios and what the leadership change could mean for the franchise's future.

title: Ten years, thousands of staff and a billion dollars: the inside story of Grand Theft Auto VI
extract: A rare inside look at Rockstar North charts a decade of GTA VI development, its enormous production scale and the creative choices behind the next Grand Theft Auto.

title: What do we actually need from the next James Bond?
extract: The Guardian's podcast asks what the next James Bond film actually needs, weighing the character's future and the expectations facing the next creative team.

title: Honey review: Killing Eve prequel drops the ball on what made the original so much fun
extract: The Killing Eve prequel Honey is reviewed as a spy-comedy that struggles to recapture the original show's sharp chemistry and dark humour.

title: The Drunkmen's Marseillaise review: a film about a secret mission to collect songs of resistance
extract: The documentary retraces a clandestine 1961 journey to record anti-Franco resistance songs in Spain, turning a little-known cultural operation into a story of musical and political defiance.
